entities.title: Gambit's HTTP API
entities.summary: The JSON routes under /games/retro/chess/api/ and auth/, with the types in shared/protocol.ts.
guarantees: Bodies are the shapes in shared/protocol.ts: Me, Lobby, Challenge, Contact, GameView with its events
Errors are JSON { error } with 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429 or 500
Responses are not cached (Cache-Control: no-store), except profile pictures (private, a day)
Every route but me needs a sign-in; a POST must be JSON from this origin
A cookie (site_session) or, for desktop builds, Authorization: Bearer identifies the player
entities.compatibility: The Worker and the Godot export deploy together, but a browser may keep an older page open across a deploy; adding fields is safe, renaming or removing them is not.

entities.title: The live connection
entities.summary: WebSocket api/games/{id}/live: the whole game after every change.
guarantees: { t: "state", game } on connecting and after every saved action
Only the game's two players may connect
entities.compatibility: LiveMessage in shared/protocol.ts also names { t: "error" }, which nothing sends; the client uses only state.

entities.title: The invitation link
entities.summary: https://…/games/retro/chess/?challenge=ID, in invitation emails and copied by players.
consumers: Invitation emails already sent, and links players have passed on
guarantees: The link opens the game, through sign-in if need be, and the lobby answers the invitation it names
The old sign-in addresses auth/login/{provider} and auth/callback/{provider} still lead to the host's sign-in
entities.compatibility: Links in sent emails cannot be changed: the path and the challenge parameter must keep working.

entities.title: The chess database
entities.summary: users, challenges, games, game_events and contacts in D1.
consumers: The GameRoom objects, which save games in it
guarantees: A game's moves are UCI moves separated by spaces; its transcript is game_events in seq order
A game against the computer has NULL for the computer's side
Users are keyed by address, as the login service gives it
entities.compatibility: schema.sql describes a fresh database; every statement can run again. The live one changes only through migrations applied by hand (docs/database-migrations.md); retire-sessions.sql, which drops the old sign-in's sessions table, is such a change but sits outside worker/migrations/.
